Duo praecepta juris una nocte expressit, neminem laeserat & honeste vixerat, sed an suum cuique reddidisset, quaeri poterat. Mutius opinor & Trebatius hoc negassent

translations.note: The joke turns on the three precepts of Roman law in Justinian: live honestly, harm no one, give each their due. 'eam' makes the bride the one who suffers from the stone, which is odd but is what the text says.
